You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Silver Acre district","question":"Can the buyer close its pre-award eligibility check?","claims":{"A":"Vale submitted a bid on lot 3.","B":"Vendor Vale held the required liability policy on 1 July.","C":"The Vale bid was submitted before the deadline."},"handoff":"The case concerns whether the buyer can close its pre-award eligibility check for Vale's bid in the Silver Acre district. The prior assessment found that Vale did not submit a bid on lot 3, as the tender portal shows a bid only on lot 2, contradicting claim A. Claim C, that the bid was submitted before the deadline, is supported by a timestamped portal record showing submission 42 minutes early. Claim B, regarding Vale holding the required liability policy on 1 July, remains unresolved because the only evidence is a draft quote conditional on payment, lacking binding proof of coverage. Thus, the key issue is the unresolved insurance status, while the lot bid and timing claims are settled.","follow_up":{"S4":"the insurer, independent of the vendor, confirms the policy was bound and active on 1 July."}}

parsed.note: Claim A is contradicted by the tender portal record showing Vale bid only on lot 2, not lot 3 (handoff). Claim C is supported by the timestamped portal record indicating submission 42 minutes before the deadline (handoff). Claim B was previously unresolved due to lack of binding proof, but the insurer's independent confirmation that the policy was bound and active on 1 July (S4) decisively supports it. Therefore, the buyer can close its pre-award eligibility check as all key eligibility criteria are met.
